# Design for the Binary Outcomes Extension

## Example Data

### Case study and target estimand

@Cro2025 use an eight-week depression trial originally reported by
@Goldstein2004. The trial compared placebo, once-daily paroxetine, and two doses of
twice-daily duloxetine. Their public example combines 100 placebo patients with
100 patients randomly selected from the three non-placebo arms. Thus, the
example's active group pools treatments.

The endpoint is a reduction of more than 50% from baseline HAMD17 at Week 8,
with earlier outcomes at Weeks 1, 2, 4, and 6. Their Table 2 targets the odds of
response on active treatment relative to placebo among trial-eligible patients
with depression, using a treatment policy strategy for early treatment cessation
(regardless of whether all assigned doses were received). The paper reports that
follow-up ceased with early treatment cessation, with 70/100 active and 61/100
placebo patients completing treatment. Table 3 gives cumulative off-treatment
percentages, which coincide with missing outcome percentages in that case study.

The data used below are the high-dropout example from the
[LSHTM Missing Data website](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/research/centres-projects-groups/missing-data#dia-missing-data), which describes these as modified demonstration data: 
the active group was sampled from the non-placebo arms, and the placebo group was expanded to 100
by resampling patients, assigning new IDs, and perturbing their outcomes.

### Import the data

The code below reads `high_low_datasets.zip` beside this document, extracting
only the high-dropout dataset, `high1.sas7bdat`, into a temporary directory.
The low-dropout dataset, `low1.sas7bdat`, is not used here.

```{r}
#| label: import-antidepressant-data
archive <- if (file.exists("high_low_datasets.zip")) {
  "high_low_datasets.zip"
} else {
  file.path("misc", "high_low_datasets.zip")
}
stopifnot(file.exists(archive))
extraction_dir <- tempfile("antidepressant-")
dir.create(extraction_dir)
sas_file <- unzip(
  archive,
  files = "high1.sas7bdat",
  exdir = extraction_dir
)
antidepressant_raw <- haven::read_sas(sas_file)
unlink(extraction_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Keep the original fields and derive the binary response without imputation.
antidepressant <- antidepressant_raw
antidepressant$arm <- factor(
  antidepressant$TRT,
  levels = c("1", "2"),
  labels = c("Placebo", "Active")
)
antidepressant$response <- with(
  antidepressant,
  as.integer(-change / basval > 0.5)
)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(antidepressant[c("PATIENT", "week")]),
  !anyNA(antidepressant$arm),
  all(antidepressant$basval > 0)
)
patients <- unique(antidepressant[c("PATIENT", "arm")])
visit_weeks <- sort(unique(antidepressant$week))
visit_weeks
```

The data set contains `r nrow(antidepressant)` observed patient-visit records for
`r length(unique(antidepressant$PATIENT))` patients, and the scheduled follow-up weeks are `r knitr::combine_words(visit_weeks)`.

```{r}
head(antidepressant)
```

- `r length(unique(antidepressant$PATIENT[antidepressant$arm == "Placebo"]))` placebo
and `r length(unique(antidepressant$PATIENT[antidepressant$arm == "Active"]))`
active
- `PATIENT` identifies patients; 
- `TRT` codes placebo as `1` and active as `2`; 
- `week` gives scheduled follow-up week; 
- `basval` is baseline HAMD17;
- `change` is follow-up minus baseline HAMD17; 
- `POOLINV` identifies the pooled investigator. 

Follow-up HAMD17 can be reconstructed as `basval + change`.
The derived binary `response` uses a strict >50% reduction from baseline,
as specified in Table 2:

```{r}
with(antidepressant, stopifnot(all(as.integer(change < -0.5 * basval) == response)))
```

There are no missing change scores in the
stored rows; missing follow-up assessments are represented by absent rows:

```{r}
stopifnot(!anyNA(antidepressant$change))
```

We use the full patient roster when calculating missingness at each visit.
The file has no separate treatment cessation indicator, so interpreting
missingness as off-treatment status relies on the case-study description in
@Cro2025.

### Check against Cro et al. Table 3

The comparison below counts observed change scores at each scheduled week,
uses the number of unique patients in each arm as the denominator, and compares
the resulting missing percentages with the published values.

```{r}
#| label: compare-table-3
comparison <- data.frame(Week = c(1, 2, 4, 6, 8))
for (arm in c("Placebo", "Active")) {
  n_arm <- sum(patients$arm == arm)
  observed <- vapply(comparison$Week, function(w) {
    sum(antidepressant$arm == arm & antidepressant$week == w &
          !is.na(antidepressant$change))
  }, integer(1))
  comparison[[paste(arm, "observed n")]] <- observed
  comparison[[paste(arm, "missing %")]] <- 100 * (n_arm - observed) / n_arm
}
comparison[["Placebo published %"]] <- c(0, 8, 15, 27, 39)
comparison[["Active published %"]] <- c(0, 10, 15, 25, 30)
stopifnot(
  all(comparison[["Placebo missing %"]] == comparison[["Placebo published %"]]),
  all(comparison[["Active missing %"]] == comparison[["Active published %"]])
)
knitr::kable(comparison, caption = "High-dropout data versus Cro et al. Table 3")
```

All entries in Table 3 are reproduced exactly. The missing percentages are
`r knitr::combine_words(comparison[["Placebo missing %"]])` for placebo and
`r knitr::combine_words(comparison[["Active missing %"]])` for active.
At Week 8, observed outcomes remain for
`r comparison[["Placebo observed n"]][comparison$Week == 8]`/
`r sum(patients$arm == "Placebo")` placebo patients and
`r comparison[["Active observed n"]][comparison$Week == 8]`/
`r sum(patients$arm == "Active")` active patients, matching the reported
completion counts.

### Response threshold discrepancy in the paper

Table 2 of @Cro2025 specifies a reduction of **more than 50%**, whereas the
Discussion describes **50% or more**. The published Week 8 responder counts
(25 placebo and 39 active) agree with the inclusive threshold in these data.
The following comparison makes the distinction explicit; `response` above
retains the strict threshold from Table 2.

```{r}
#| label: compare-response-thresholds
threshold_comparison <- antidepressant |> 
  dplyr::filter(week == 8) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Reduction >50%` = sum(response, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Reduction >=50%` = sum(-change / basval >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Arm = arm) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Published responders` = c(25L, 39L))
stopifnot(
  all(threshold_comparison[["Reduction >=50%"]] ==
        threshold_comparison[["Published responders"]])
)
knitr::kable(threshold_comparison, caption = "Week 8 responders by threshold")
```

So we see that replicating the paper's reported responder counts requires
the inclusive threshold.

## Cro et al. latent multivariate probit reference implementation

The separate file `cro_latent_mvn_reference.R` preserves the supplied supplementary code from @Cro2025. 
It includes the original trial-specific analysis and is retained for reference; source the
lightly edited file `cro_latent_mvn.R`, which includes an R function, to run the imputation algorithm.
The wrapper requires the `jomo`, `mice`, and `gear` packages from CRAN. It exposes the original
settings as arguments and returns the binary imputations (`imp`), latent draws
(`impZ`), and retained arm-specific regression and covariance draws (`beta` and
`omega`). It omits the final trial-specific pooled GLM. The wrapper converts `Ycat` to
a data frame before the original factor-conversion loop so that factor levels
are retained when the caller supplies a matrix.

### Prepare the longitudinal binary outcomes

Create one row per patient and one column per scheduled visit, leaving absent
visits as `NA`. Treatment is coded 1 for placebo (reference) and 2 for active.
We retain the strict response threshold defined above. This prepares inputs for
a future implementation comparison, rather than reproducing the paper's
inclusive-threshold responder counts.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-cro-probit-inputs
cro_script <- file.path(dirname(archive), "cro_latent_mvn.R")
source(cro_script)
Ycat <- matrix(
  NA_integer_, 
  nrow = nrow(patients), 
  ncol = length(visit_weeks),
  dimnames = list(
    as.character(patients$PATIENT), 
    paste0("week", visit_weeks)
  )
)
Ycat[cbind(
  match(antidepressant$PATIENT, patients$PATIENT),
  match(antidepressant$week, visit_weeks)
)] <- antidepressant$response
treat1 <- as.integer(patients$arm)
stopifnot(
  all(treat1 %in% 1:2),
  all(Ycat[!is.na(Ycat)] %in% 0:1),
  all(colSums(is.na(Ycat)) == c(0, 18, 30, 52, 69))
)
```

### Run a short example

This short J2R run demonstrates successful execution only; its chain is too short for
inference. For the supplementary settings use `nburn = 500`, `nbetween = 500`,
and `nimp = 1000`. The original internal seed is exposed as `seed`, retaining
its default of 123435. The supplementary code uses the latent sign convention
**Y = 0 when Z > 0**, which must be accounted for in future comparisons.
The algorithm is retained as supplied, including its intercept-only imputation
step and reference-group handling; the example uses monotone dropout and
reference arm 1. It has not been generalized to other input configurations.

```{r}
#| label: run-cro-probit-example
cro_draws <- cro_latent_mvn(
  Ycat = Ycat, 
  treat1 = treat1, 
  Method = "J2R", 
  Reference = 1,
  nburn = 100, 
  nbetween = 10, 
  nimp = 5, 
  seed = 123435
)
# Imputation 0 contains the original data; positive indices are completed data.
cro_completed <- subset(cro_draws$imp, Imputation == 1)
stopifnot(
  nrow(cro_completed) == nrow(Ycat),
  !anyNA(cro_completed[colnames(Ycat)]),
  all(as.matrix(cro_completed[colnames(Ycat)])[!is.na(Ycat)] ==
        Ycat[!is.na(Ycat)])
)
knitr::kable(
  aggregate(week8 ~ Imputation + Treat, data = cro_draws$imp,
            FUN = mean, subset = Imputation > 0),
  caption = "Week 8 response proportions in the short J2R example"
)
# Retained parameter draws for the subsequent rbmi comparison:
dim(cro_draws$beta$reference)
dim(cro_draws$omega$active)
```

For incomplete patients, `impZ` contains sequential latent draws at all visits;
its imputation-0 block contains the original binary data, and complete patients'
latent rows remain zero in the supplied algorithm. Use latent rows only for
patients with missing outcomes and positive imputation indices.

## Multivariate Probit Draw Model Implemented with Stan

### Scope and statistical target

This is a draw-step prototype for binary outcomes. The target is
Section 3.3 of @Cro2025, rather than numerical behavior specific to the supplied
R code. Preparation, posterior sampling, and parameter
extraction are separate operations to stay within the `rbmi` framework.

To connect with Section 3.3, let a superscript $\mathrm{P}$ distinguish the
paper's latent variables and parameters from those used below. The paper indexes
arm by $t\in\{a,r\}$ and writes the model componentwise as

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,i,j}&=\mu^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,j}+e^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,i,j},&
e^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,i}&\sim N_D(0,\Omega^{\mathrm{P}}_t),\\
Y_{t,i,j}&=\mathbf{1}(Z^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,i,j}\leq 0),&
\operatorname{diag}(\Omega^{\mathrm{P}}_t)&=\mathbf{1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Equivalently, the subject's latent vector has distribution
$Z^{\mathrm{P}}_{t,i}\sim N_D(\mu^{\mathrm{P}}_t,\Omega^{\mathrm{P}}_t)$.
Section 3.3 also uses $\Sigma_t$ for this same latent covariance matrix;
we consistently use $\Omega$. With unit diagonal it is also a correlation matrix.
Here $D$ counts the modeled binary visits: it corresponds to the paper's $J+1$
when the same visits are included. The paper includes a baseline response in
that indexing; the example here models only the five follow-up binary responses,
so $D=5$, with baseline HAMD17 available as a separate covariate.

For the implementation, index subjects across arms and let $a_i$ denote subject
$i$'s randomized arm (the paper's $t$). Conditional on the supplied design rows
$x_{ij}$, use

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_i \mid \beta,\Omega&\sim N_D(\mu_i,\Omega_{a_i}),&
\mu_{ij}&=x_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\beta,\\
Y_{ij}&=\mathbf{1}(Z_{ij}>0),&
\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_t)&=\mathbf{1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For the arm-by-visit model, the two formulations are related by the global sign change

$$
Z_{ij}=-Z^{\mathrm{P}}_{a_i,i,j},\qquad
\mu_{ij}=-\mu^{\mathrm{P}}_{a_i,j},\qquad
\Omega_t=\Omega^{\mathrm{P}}_t.
$$

The binary outcomes are unchanged (the boundary $Z=0$ has probability zero).
Thus $\Pr(Y_{ij}=1\mid\beta)=\Phi(\mu_{ij}) =\Phi(-\mu^{\mathrm{P}}_{a_i,j})$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF.
Negating every latent component preserves all covariances and correlations.

The default design has one intercept per arm and visit: $x_{ij}$ selects
coefficient $\beta_{a_i,j}$ from the vector $\beta$, which stacks one block per arm,
where
$\beta_t=(\beta_{t,1},\ldots,\beta_{t,D})^{\mathsf T}$. Consequently
$\mu_{ij}=\beta_{a_i,j}=-\mu^{\mathrm{P}}_{a_i,j}$ in this design.
Writing a single $\beta$ therefore still gives separate arm-specific means;
with the independent priors below, the default posterior factors by arm, just
as in the paper, with separate unstructured correlation matrices.
A common correlation matrix (`same_cov = TRUE`) and a supplied covariate design
are also supported. Covariates enter through $x_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\beta$;
arm-by-visit interactions allow the separate visit-specific covariate effects
described in the paper, while shared coefficients impose additional assumptions.
The default design includes no baseline covariate. A common correlation matrix
is an extension beyond the paper's separate-arm model; treatment means remain
separate when `same_cov = TRUE`. Binary observations identify correlations,
not unrestricted latent variances.

The supplementary code follows the paper's sign convention. Consequently compare
**Stan's $\beta$ with minus Cro's $\beta$**, after matching the design and
coefficient order, while leaving the correlation matrices unchanged.

The priors matching the latent model in Section 3.3 are
$p(\beta)\propto1$ and $\Omega_t\sim\operatorname{LKJ}(1)$, independently by arm.
The paper describes flat priors for that model and fixes every latent variance
to one. The Jeffreys covariance prior occurs in Section 3.2, which instead
fits an unrestricted MVN model directly to the binary outcomes as if they were
continuous, followed by adaptive rounding. These are different models and prior
specifications; the Jeffreys choice in Section 3.2 is not the covariance prior
specified for the latent probit method.

To make the equivalence with the Section 3.3 flat prior explicit, let
$\mathcal C_D$ be the space of positive definite $D\times D$ matrices with unit
diagonal. With density measured against the free off-diagonal entries,

$$
p(\Omega_t\mid\eta)\propto
\det(\Omega_t)^{\eta-1}\mathbf{1}(\Omega_t\in\mathcal C_D).
$$

Thus $\eta=1$ is exactly a constant density on the admissible correlation
matrices. This prior is proper because $\mathcal C_D$ has finite volume. The
paper's description of the latent covariance prior as improper is therefore
imprecise once the diagonal is fixed; the flat mean prior remains improper.

`beta_sd = 0` requests flat coefficient priors. The preparation function
allows this only for the saturated arm-by-visit design, with both binary outcomes
observed in every arm and visit. For a custom design, specify `beta_sd > 0`, giving
independent $N(0,\texttt{beta\_sd}^2)$ priors. This avoids silently using an improper
posterior under separation. It is then a different prior from the paper. The
prototype does not choose a universal prior scale for future package integration.

### Observed-data likelihood and returned draws

Let $O_i$ be the observed visits. The fitted likelihood is the probability that
the latent signs match the observed outcomes:

$$
L_i(\beta,\Omega)=
\Pr\!\left((2Y_{ij}-1)Z_{ij}>0\text{ for all }j\in O_i
\mid\beta,\Omega\right).
$$

Missing visits are integrated out analytically before augmentation. Patients
with no observed visits contribute one and are omitted from the likelihood,
while their indices are retained in metadata. Monotone dropout is not required.
In a later package implementation, the draw-stage data policy must determine
which post-ICE observations to exclude; this prototype treats exactly the cells
supplied as observed as its fitting data.

The returned draws contain coefficients and latent correlation matrices only.
MAR/J2R/CR/CIR/LMCF assumptions belong to the later imputation step and must not
feed back into this posterior. In particular, the auxiliary variables sampled
below are computational devices, **not completed outcomes or latent values to
reuse under a reference-based imputation assumption**. That step will need its
own conditional latent sampling, respecting the observed binary signs. Agreement
here does not validate the reference code's subsequent imputation algorithm or
reproduce its pooled treatment-effect table.

### Stan implementation and parameterization

The [Stan multivariate probit example](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/regression.html#multivariate-probit-regression)
augments the likelihood with sign-constrained normal variables. The same model
can be expressed using uniform variables and conditional normal quantiles. The
underlying transformation of multivariate normal probabilities to integrals over
the unit cube is described by @Genz1992. For multivariate probit specifically,
@Goodrich2016 implemented this parameterization in Stan's `probit-multi-good.stan`
example. His [accompanying explanation](https://groups.google.com/g/stan-users/c/G3HAQ3dp1f8)
describes the sequential quantile transformation and its Jacobian adjustment,
also motivated by low BFMI in the sign-constrained formulation. A published
extension to dichotomous and ordinal diagnostic tests builds on Goodrich's code
[@Cerullo2022, Section 3.5 and Supplementary Material 5].

We use this equivalent parameterization below because the direct sign-constrained
version had low E-BFMI and divergences in an initial fit to this example. With the
change-of-variables adjustment included, it preserves the marginal posterior for
$\beta$ and $\Omega$.

For the observed subvector of a patient, let $L L^{\mathsf T}=\Omega[O_i,O_i]$,
where $O_i = \{j: Y_{ij} \text{ is observed}\}$, as well as
$s_j=2Y_{ij}-1$, $Z=\mu+Le$, and

$$
c_j=\mu_j+\sum_{k<j}L_{jk}e_k,\quad
p_j=\Phi(s_jc_j/L_{jj}),\quad
u_j\in(0,1),\quad e_j=-s_j\Phi^{-1}(u_jp_j).
$$

The change of variables from sign-constrained $Z$ to $u$ has Jacobian that
cancels the conditional normal density except for $p_j$. Hence the augmented
target contributes $\sum_j\log p_j$, with independent uniform base measures for
$u$. Integrating out $u$ recovers the likelihood above. We implement
$u_j=\Phi(v_j)$ with $v_j\sim N(0,1)$ for unconstrained auxiliary parameters.
These variables are parameters sampled jointly with $\beta$ and $\Omega$, not newly simulated
numbers inserted into an approximate likelihood. The final uniform for each
subject has no effect on the weight and is integrated out, leaving
$\sum_i(|O_i|-1)$ auxiliary parameters. A one-visit patient needs none. The internal
calculation uses reverse visit order; this changes sampling efficiency, not the
joint likelihood or the visit labels in the returned matrices.

Patients sharing an observed-visit pattern and a covariance group share a matrix
factorization. We factor the principal submatrix of $\Omega$; simply taking
the corresponding rows and columns of its full Cholesky factor would generally
be wrong. Probabilities are computed using `normal_lcdf`, without probability
clipping or `Phi_approx`. The helper computes normal quantiles from log
probabilities: it uses symmetry
and, in the far tail, six Newton updates of the log-CDF equation. This avoids
exponentiating extremely small probabilities or subtracting them from one.
Invalid proposals at floating-point singularities are still rejected by Stan.
This is a prototype for
moderate-dimensional longitudinal data, not a claim of robust sampling for
arbitrary rare outcomes, separation, or nearly singular correlations.

All implementation functions below are evaluated when rendering. The expensive
fits and the isolated rebuild of the reference sampler are opt-in. From the
repository root, run 

```bash
RBMI_RUN_PROBIT_VALIDATION=true quarto render misc/design_binary_extension.qmd --to html
```

to recompute them. The recorded
results later in this section are a fixed validation snapshot, not output from
the earlier five-imputation illustration. Dependencies are `cmdstanr` with a
working CmdStan C++ toolchain, `posterior`, `mvtnorm`, and the earlier example's
R dependencies. Corrected-reference validation also needs access to the jomo
2.7-6 source archive and an R package compilation toolchain.

First let's check whether we want to run the probit validation:

```{r}
#| label: probit-run-settings
run_probit_validation <- identical(Sys.getenv("RBMI_RUN_PROBIT_VALIDATION"), "true")
```

Here comes the Stan source code for the probit model:

```{r}
#| label: probit-stan-source
probit_stan_code <- r"(
functions {
  // Normal quantile from a log probability, without tail clipping.
  real std_normal_quantile_log(real lp) {
    real small_lp = lp < log(0.5) ? lp : log1m_exp(lp);
    real q;
    if (small_lp > -36) {
      q = inv_Phi(exp(small_lp));
    } else {
      q = -sqrt(-2 * small_lp);
      for (k in 1:6) {
        real lcdf = normal_lcdf(q | 0, 1);
        q -= (lcdf - small_lp) * exp(lcdf - normal_lpdf(q | 0, 1));
      }
    }
    return lp < log(0.5) ? q : -q;
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=1> D; // number of visits
  int<lower=1> P; // number of predictors
  int<lower=1> G; // number of covariance groups
  int<lower=1> R; // number of rows in the design matrix
  int<lower=1> B; // number of blocks
  int<lower=0> U; // number of auxiliary variables
  matrix[R, P] X; // design matrix
  vector[R] sign_y; // observed signs of the response
  array[B] int<lower=1, upper=D> K; // number of visits per block
  array[B, D] int<lower=1, upper=D> visit; // visit indices for each block
  array[B] int<lower=1> n_subject; // number of subjects per block
  array[B] int<lower=1, upper=R> start; // starting row index for each block
  array[B] int<lower=1, upper=G> cov_group; // covariance group for each block
  real<lower=0> beta_sd; // zero selects a flat coefficient prior
  real<lower=0> lkj_eta; // LKJ correlation prior parameter
}
parameters {
  vector[P] beta; // regression coefficients
  array[G] cholesky_factor_corr[D] L_Omega; // Cholesky factors of correlation matrices
  vector[U] u_raw; // auxiliary variables
}
transformed parameters {
  array[G] corr_matrix[D] Omega; // correlation matrices for each group
  for (g in 1:G) // compute correlation matrix for each group from its Cholesky factor
    Omega[g] = multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose(L_Omega[g]);
}
model {
  vector[R] mu = X * beta; // linear predictor for each row
  int u_pos = 1; // initialize position index for auxiliary variables in u_raw
  u_raw ~ std_normal(); // prior for auxiliary variables
  if (beta_sd > 0) beta ~ normal(0, beta_sd); // prior for regression coefficients
  for (g in 1:G) L_Omega[g] ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(lkj_eta); // prior for Cholesky factors of correlation matrices
  for (b in 1:B) { // loop over blocks
    array[K[b]] int v = visit[b, 1:K[b]]; // visit indices for this block
    matrix[K[b], K[b]] L = cholesky_decompose( // Cholesky factor for this block's covariance submatrix
      Omega[cov_group[b]][v, v]);
    for (i in 1:n_subject[b]) { // loop over subjects within this block
      vector[K[b] - 1] e; // auxiliary vector for conditional calculations
      for (j in 1:K[b]) { // loop over visits within this subject
        int r = start[b] + (i - 1) * K[b] + j - 1; // row index for this observation
        real conditional_mu = mu[r]; // conditional mean for this observation
        real log_mass; // log CDF mass for this observation
        if (j > 1) conditional_mu += L[j, 1:(j - 1)] * head(e, j - 1); // update conditional mean
        log_mass = normal_lcdf(sign_y[r] * conditional_mu / L[j, j] | 0, 1); // compute log CDF
        target += log_mass; // increment target with log mass
        if (j < K[b]) { // update auxiliary vector for next step if not the last visit
          e[j] = -sign_y[r] * std_normal_quantile_log(normal_lcdf(u_raw[u_pos] | 0, 1) + log_mass);
          u_pos += 1; // move to next auxiliary variable
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
)"
```

### R preparation, fitting, and extraction

`X`, when supplied, is an $N\times D\times P$ array: a design row for every
subject and visit. This permits shared coefficients, arm effects, visit effects,
and interactions without imposing a formula interface at this stage. Covariates
must be complete and numeric. `cells` records the mapping from Stan's observed
rows back to the input matrix; `visit_names` fixes the longitudinal order.
The default coefficient order is arm first, then visit.

For this strongly correlated example, the fit helper first adapts the NUTS metric,
then starts sampling from each chain's final state with the learned metric and a
step size no larger than 0.005. The adaptation-stage iteration is discarded.
This conservative cap costs runtime but addresses divergences that remained with
ordinary step-size adaptation. It is a tuning choice, not a modification of the
model. Final diagnostics still need to be checked on every new dataset. CmdStanR
is used here for convenient standalone compilation; integration with the package's
existing RStan infrastructure is deferred.

`extract_probit_draws()` returns a list of coefficient vectors and a paired list
of covariance-group matrices, analogous to the count prototype's parameter-only
extraction. It does not construct a package `draws` object. It samples retained
iterations without replacement; it never samples coefficients and correlations
independently. Keep the complete fitted chains for convergence diagnostics,
even when fewer draws are requested for downstream imputation.

```{r}
#| label: probit-r-functions
prepare_probit_data <- function(Y, arm, X = NULL, same_cov = FALSE,
                                beta_sd = 0, lkj_eta = 1) {
  Y <- as.matrix(Y)
  stopifnot(is.numeric(Y), length(dim(Y)) == 2L,
            nrow(Y) > 0L, ncol(Y) > 0L,
            all(Y[!is.na(Y)] %in% 0:1), length(arm) == nrow(Y),
            !anyNA(arm), length(same_cov) == 1L, is.logical(same_cov),
            !is.na(same_cov), length(beta_sd) == 1L,
            is.finite(beta_sd), beta_sd >= 0,
            length(lkj_eta) == 1L, is.finite(lkj_eta), lkj_eta > 0)
  arm <- droplevels(factor(arm))
  N <- nrow(Y); D <- ncol(Y); A <- nlevels(arm)
  saturated <- is.null(X)
  if (saturated) {
    # X[i, d, p] gives subject i's design row at visit d.
    X <- array(0, c(N, D, A * D))
    for (i in seq_len(N)) for (d in seq_len(D))
      X[i, d, (as.integer(arm[i]) - 1L) * D + d] <- 1
    coefficient_names <- paste(rep(levels(arm), each = D),
                               rep(colnames(Y) %||% seq_len(D), A), sep = ":")
  } else {
    stopifnot(is.array(X), length(dim(X)) == 3L,
              identical(dim(X)[1:2], c(N, D)), dim(X)[3] > 0L,
              is.numeric(X), all(is.finite(X)))
    coefficient_names <- dimnames(X)[[3]] %||% paste0("beta", seq_len(dim(X)[3]))
  }
  if (beta_sd == 0) {
    if (!saturated) stop("Use a proper beta_sd > 0 with a custom design.")
    for (a in levels(arm)) for (d in seq_len(D)) {
      yy <- Y[arm == a, d]
      if (!all(0:1 %in% yy))
        stop("Flat priors require both outcomes in every arm and visit.")
    }
  }
  observed <- !is.na(Y)
  keep <- which(rowSums(observed) > 0L)
  if (!length(keep)) stop("No observed outcomes.")
  cg <- if (same_cov) rep(1L, N) else as.integer(arm)
  # Group patients by covariance group and arbitrary observed-visit pattern.
  key <- paste(cg, apply(observed, 1, paste0, collapse = ""), sep = ":")
  blocks <- split(keep, factor(key[keep], levels = unique(key[keep])))
  K <- vapply(blocks, function(ii) sum(observed[ii[1], ]), integer(1))
  n_subject <- lengths(blocks)
  visit <- matrix(1L, length(blocks), D)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(blocks), function(b) {
    ii <- blocks[[b]]
    # Reverse only the internal integration order; output visit order is unchanged.
    vv <- rev(which(observed[ii[1], ]))
    visit[b, seq_along(vv)] <<- vv
    cbind(subject = rep(ii, each = length(vv)), visit = rep(vv, length(ii)))
  })
  cells <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  P <- dim(X)[3]
  x_obs <- vapply(seq_len(P), function(p) matrix(X[, , p], N, D)[cells], numeric(nrow(cells)))
  x_obs <- matrix(x_obs, nrow(cells), P)
  y_obs <- Y[cells]
  if (qr(x_obs)$rank < P && beta_sd == 0) stop("Rank-deficient flat-prior design.")
  data <- list(D = D, P = P, G = if (same_cov) 1L else A,
               R = length(y_obs), B = length(blocks), U = length(y_obs) - length(keep), X = x_obs,
               sign_y = 2 * y_obs - 1,
               K = unname(K), visit = visit, n_subject = unname(n_subject),
               start = as.integer(cumsum(c(1L, head(K * n_subject, -1L)))),
               cov_group = vapply(blocks, function(ii) cg[ii[1]], integer(1)),
               beta_sd = beta_sd, lkj_eta = lkj_eta)
  list(data = data, coefficient_names = coefficient_names,
       arm_levels = levels(arm), visit_names = colnames(Y) %||% as.character(seq_len(D)),
       cells = cells, excluded_subjects = setdiff(seq_len(N), keep),
       same_cov = same_cov, saturated = saturated)
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

fit_probit_draws <- function(prepared, model, chains = 4L, parallel_chains = chains,
                            iter_warmup = 1500L, iter_sampling = 2000L,
                            seed = 20261026L, adapt_delta = 0.99,
                            step_size_cap = 0.005, ...) {
  stopifnot(length(step_size_cap) == 1L, is.finite(step_size_cap), step_size_cap > 0)
  # Adapt the metric, then sample with a conservative fixed step size.
  warm <- model$sample(data = prepared$data, chains = chains,
    parallel_chains = parallel_chains, iter_warmup = iter_warmup,
    iter_sampling = 1L, seed = seed, adapt_delta = adapt_delta,
    max_treedepth = 12L, step_size = 0.05, refresh = 0, sig_figs = 18, diagnostics = NULL, ...)
  dat <- prepared$data
  variables <- c("beta", "L_Omega", if (dat$U > 0L) "u_raw")
  d <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(warm$draws(variables))
  initial <- lapply(seq_len(chains), function(ch) list(
    beta = as.numeric(d[ch, paste0("beta[", seq_len(dat$P), "]")]),
    L_Omega = lapply(seq_len(dat$G), function(g) {
      nm <- outer(seq_len(dat$D), seq_len(dat$D), function(j, k)
        sprintf("L_Omega[%d,%d,%d]", g, j, k))
      matrix(as.numeric(d[ch, as.vector(nm)]), dat$D, dat$D)
    }),
    u_raw = if (dat$U > 0L) as.numeric(d[ch, paste0("u_raw[", seq_len(dat$U), "]")]) else numeric()
  ))
  fit <- model$sample(data = dat, chains = chains, parallel_chains = parallel_chains,
    iter_warmup = 0L, iter_sampling = iter_sampling, seed = seed + 1L,
    init = initial, metric = "diag_e", inv_metric = warm$inv_metric(matrix = FALSE),
    adapt_engaged = FALSE,
    step_size = pmin(step_size_cap, warm$metadata()$step_size_adaptation),
    max_treedepth = 12L, refresh = 0)
  structure(list(fit = fit, warmup_fit = warm, prepared = prepared), class = "probit_draw_fit")
}

extract_probit_draws <- function(object, n_samples = NULL, seed = 123L) {
  # Select paired beta/Omega rows; retain full chains in object$fit for diagnostics.
  d <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(object$fit$draws(c("beta", "Omega")))
  if (is.null(n_samples)) n_samples <- nrow(d)
  stopifnot(length(n_samples) == 1L, is.finite(n_samples), n_samples >= 1L,
            n_samples == as.integer(n_samples), n_samples <= nrow(d))
  set.seed(seed)
  take <- sample.int(nrow(d), n_samples, replace = FALSE)
  dat <- object$prepared$data
  beta <- lapply(take, function(i) setNames(
    as.numeric(d[i, paste0("beta[", seq_len(dat$P), "]")]),
    object$prepared$coefficient_names))
  sigma <- lapply(take, function(i) lapply(seq_len(dat$G), function(g) {
    nm <- outer(seq_len(dat$D), seq_len(dat$D), function(j, k)
      sprintf("Omega[%d,%d,%d]", g, j, k))
    matrix(as.numeric(d[i, as.vector(nm)]), dat$D, dat$D,
           dimnames = rep(list(object$prepared$visit_names), 2))
  }))
  list(beta = beta, sigma = sigma, metadata = object$prepared[
    c("coefficient_names", "arm_levels", "visit_names", "same_cov")])
}
```

probit_input <- prepare_probit_data(Ycat, treat1, same_cov = FALSE)
stopifnot(probit_input$data$R == 831L, probit_input$data$U == 631L)

          length(probit_parameters$sigma[[1]]) == 2L)

### Audit of the reference draw sampler

The comparison calls `jomo::jomo1cat.MCMCchain()` separately by arm, exactly as
in the draw-stage calls inside `cro_latent_mvn()`. It skips the subsequent
imputation loops. Thus the short J2R run above is not used to assess posterior
agreement. Both methods use the same **strict >50% response threshold**, the same
200 patients, and the same observed visits.

#### Which covariance prior does the reference code use?

In `cro_latent_mvn_reference.R`, the two `jomo1cat.MCMCchain()` calls pass
`l1cov.start` but do not pass `l1cov.prior`, although the script defines that
object. `l1cov.start` initializes the matrix; it does not specify a prior.
The [jomo R wrapper](https://github.com/cran/jomo/blob/2.7-6/R/jomo1cat.MCMCchain.R)
defaults `l1cov.prior` to the identity and passes it to C as `Sp`. However, in
the [jomo 2.7-6 C source](https://github.com/cran/jomo/blob/2.7-6/src/jomo1C.c),
`Sp` enters only the `ncat == 0` covariance-update branch. Binary outcomes use
the categorical branch, where the diagonal is fixed to one and the acceptance
ratio uses only the augmented normal likelihood,

$$
\ell(\Omega_t)=-\frac{n_t}{2}\log|\Omega_t|
-\frac12\sum_i (z_{t,i}-\mu_{t,i})^{\mathsf T}
\Omega_t^{-1}(z_{t,i}-\mu_{t,i}).
$$

There is no additional Jeffreys determinant term or inverse-Wishart prior term.
The determinant term shown here belongs to the **likelihood**, not the prior.
Our source-level interpretation is that the intended binary prior is flat in
the free correlations, consistent with Section 3.3 and LKJ(1). Passing a different
`l1cov.prior` does not change this binary covariance update. This conclusion
concerns the intended prior, rather than correctness of the complete sampler:
the implementation has the two issues below.

#### Departures from the intended binary sampler

The [jomo 2.7-6 source](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/jomo/jomo_2.7-6.tar.gz),
`src/jomo1C.c`, reveals two departures from the intended binary sampler:

1. Observed latent proposals must lie in $(-3,4)$ as well as satisfy their sign.
   These finite bounds change the augmentation target; they are not in the
   paper's probit model. Under our opposite sign convention the bounds would be
   $(-4,3)$. The limit of 10,000 rejection attempts is also unnecessary for a
   binary truncated normal.
2. A correlation proposal is repeatedly redrawn until the matrix is positive
   definite (up to 100 tries), then accepted using only a likelihood ratio.
   Conditioning a symmetric normal proposal on this feasible interval makes
   its normalization depend on the current correlation. The missing proposal
   ratio can therefore change the stationary distribution.

The second point follows directly from the proposal construction. If the
feasible interval for a correlation is $(l,h)$ and the proposal scale is $s$,
its acceptance probability must account for
$A(r)=\Phi((h-r)/s)-\Phi((l-r)/s)$. Retrying until feasible gives
$q(r'\mid r)=\phi((r'-r)/s)/(sA(r))$, requiring an additional
$A(r)/A(r')$ in the Metropolis ratio. Instead, the patch below uses one symmetric
proposal and rejects it immediately if invalid. For binary observations it
also draws the exact one-sided conditional normal using log-tail quantiles.
Neither correction changes the intended flat priors. The categorical covariance
update uses no inverse-Wishart term from `l1cov.prior`; supplying that argument
is not a substitute for specifying the correlation prior here.

These corrections are deliberately limited to the binary draw model. They are
not a general repair of jomo's mixed-outcome samplers. The original reference
files and the installed jomo package are preserved: the helper builds a patched
copy in a temporary library and runs it in a separate R process. The patch checks
the source version and expected edit locations and fails if they do not match.

```{r}
#| label: patch-binary-reference
patch_jomo_binary <- function(source_dir) {
  path <- file.path(source_dir, "src", "jomo1C.c")
  lines <- readLines(path)
  stopifnot(read.dcf(file.path(source_dir, "DESCRIPTION"))[1, "Version"] == "2.7-6")
  # For binary categories only, exact one-sided conditional normal draws.
  first <- grep("if (REAL(Y)[t+(ncon+j)*IY]==INTEGER(Y_numcat)[j])", lines, fixed=TRUE)
  last <- grep("//Updating beta", lines, fixed=TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(first)==1L, length(last)==1L, last > first)
  end <- first + which(trimws(lines[(first+1L):(last-1L)]) == "flag=0;")[1]
  old <- lines[first:(end-1L)]
  replacement <- c(
    "if (currncat == 1) {",
    "  int lower_tail = (REAL(Y)[t+(ncon+j)*IY] == 2);",
    "  double sd = sqrt(omegadrawmiss[0]);",
    "  double lp = pnorm5(0, mumiss[0], sd, lower_tail, 1);",
    "  imp[t+pos*IY] = qnorm5(log(unif_rand()) + lp, mumiss[0], sd, lower_tail, 1);",
    "} else {", old, "}")
  lines <- c(lines[seq_len(first-1L)], replacement, lines[end:length(lines)])
  # One symmetric proposal. Reject invalid matrices before factorization.
  first <- grep("while ((flag==0)&(kk<100))", lines, fixed=TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(first)==1L)
  end <- first + which(trimws(lines[(first+1L):length(lines)]) == "}")[1]
  replacement <- c(
    "newomega[j+JY*k] = r8_normal_sample(meanom,sdom,0);",
    "newomega[k+JY*j] = newomega[j+JY*k];",
    "flag = checkposdef(JY,newomega,help,help5);",
    "if (flag == 0) {",
    "  newomega[j+JY*k] = REAL(omega)[j+JY*k];",
    "  newomega[k+JY*j] = REAL(omega)[k+JY*j];",
    "  continue;",
    "}")
  lines <- c(lines[seq_len(first-1L)], replacement, lines[(end+1L):length(lines)])
  writeLines(lines, path)
  invisible(path)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: reference-draw-functions
run_reference_chain <- function(chain, input) {
  set.seed(input$seed + chain)
  lapply(seq_len(nlevels(factor(input$arm))), function(a) {
    yy <- as.data.frame(input$Y[as.integer(factor(input$arm)) == a, , drop = FALSE])
    yy[] <- lapply(yy, factor, levels = 0:1)
    # Mirrors Cro's two draw-stage jomo calls; no reference-based imputation.
    f <- jomo::jomo1cat.MCMCchain(
      Y.cat = yy, Y.numcat = rep(2L, ncol(yy)),
      nburn = input$warmup + input$iterations, output = 0
    )
    take <- seq.int(input$warmup + input$thin,
                    input$warmup + input$iterations, by = input$thin)
    list(beta = f$collectbeta[, , take, drop = FALSE],
         omega = f$collectomega[, , take, drop = FALSE])
  })
}

run_reference_draws <- function(Y, arm, library = NULL, chains = 4L,
                                warmup = 100000L, iterations = 1000000L,
                                thin = 100L, seed = 123435L) {
  stopifnot(ncol(Y) >= 2L, length(arm) == nrow(Y), !anyNA(arm),
            all(Y[!is.na(Y)] %in% 0:1), chains >= 1L,
            warmup >= 1L, iterations >= thin, thin >= 1L)
  # This comparison adapter deliberately stays within Cro's example scope.
  for (a in unique(arm)) {
    yy <- Y[arm == a, , drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(anyNA(yy), all(rowSums(!is.na(yy)) > 0L),
              all(vapply(seq_len(ncol(yy)), function(j)
                all(0:1 %in% yy[, j]), logical(1))))
  }
  work <- tempfile("probit-reference-")
  dir.create(work)
  on.exit(unlink(work, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  input <- list(Y = Y, arm = arm, library = library, chains = chains,
                warmup = warmup, iterations = iterations, thin = thin, seed = seed)
  input_path <- file.path(work, "input.rds")
  output_path <- file.path(work, "output.rds")
  script_path <- file.path(work, "run.R")
  log_path <- file.path(work, "run.log")
  saveRDS(input, input_path)
  writeLines(c("run_chain <-", deparse(run_reference_chain),
    "args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)",
    "input <- readRDS(args[1])",
    "if (!is.null(input$library)) .libPaths(c(input$library, .libPaths()))",
    "stopifnot(as.character(utils::packageVersion('jomo')) == '2.7.6')",
    "cores <- if (.Platform$OS.type == 'windows') 1L else input$chains",
    "out <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(input$chains), run_chain, input = input, mc.cores = cores)",
    "if (any(vapply(out, inherits, logical(1), 'try-error'))) stop('Reference chain failed')",
    "saveRDS(out, args[2])"), script_path)
  status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
                    shQuote(c(script_path, input_path, output_path)),
                    stdout = log_path, stderr = log_path)
  if (status != 0L) stop(paste(readLines(log_path), collapse = "\n"))
  readRDS(output_path)
}

build_corrected_jomo <- function(archive = NULL) {
  work <- tempfile("jomo-binary-audit-")
  dir.create(work)
  if (is.null(archive)) {
    archive <- file.path(work, "jomo_2.7-6.tar.gz")
    urls <- c(
      "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/jomo_2.7-6.tar.gz",
      "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/jomo/jomo_2.7-6.tar.gz")
    downloaded <- FALSE
    for (url in urls) {
      status <- try(suppressWarnings(utils::download.file(
        url, archive, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)), silent = TRUE)
      if (!inherits(status, "try-error") && status == 0L) {
        downloaded <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    if (!downloaded) stop("Supply the jomo 2.7-6 source archive locally.")
  }
  utils::untar(archive, exdir = work)
  src <- file.path(work, "jomo")
  patch_jomo_binary(src)
  lib <- file.path(work, "library")
  dir.create(lib)
  log <- file.path(work, "install.log")
  status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"),
                    c("CMD", "INSTALL", "-l", shQuote(lib), shQuote(src)),
                    stdout = log, stderr = log)
  if (status != 0L) stop(paste(readLines(log), collapse = "\n"))
  lib
}
```

The reference runner discards 100,000 sweeps and retains every 100th sweep from
one million subsequent sweeps, for each of four independent chains per arm.
This thinning limits storage; it does not establish independence. Correlation
mixing, rather than coefficient mixing, determines how long these runs need to
be. All signs, parameter ordering, MCSEs, and diagnostics are harmonized below.
The comparison includes all ten coefficients and twenty distinct correlations;
constant diagonal entries and duplicated upper triangles are excluded.

```{r}
#| label: compare-probit-functions
jomo_array <- function(chains) {
  S <- dim(chains[[1]][[1]]$beta)[3]
  A <- length(chains[[1]])
  D <- dim(chains[[1]][[1]]$omega)[1]
  pair <- which(lower.tri(matrix(0,D,D)),arr.ind=TRUE)
  nm <- c(paste0("beta[",seq_len(A*D),"]"), unlist(lapply(seq_len(A),function(a)
    sprintf("Omega[%d,%d,%d]",a,pair[,1],pair[,2]))))
  arr <- array(NA_real_,c(S,length(chains),length(nm)),dimnames=list(NULL,NULL,nm))
  for (ch in seq_along(chains)) {
    values <- c(lapply(seq_len(A),function(a) -t(chains[[ch]][[a]]$beta[1,,])),
                lapply(seq_len(A),function(a) t(vapply(seq_len(S), function(s)
                  chains[[ch]][[a]]$omega[,,s][pair], numeric(nrow(pair))))))
    arr[,ch,] <- do.call(cbind,values)
  }
  posterior::as_draws_array(arr)
}
summarize_parameters <- function(draws) {
  as.data.frame(posterior::summarise_draws(draws, mean=mean, sd=sd,
    q025=function(x) unname(quantile(x,.025)),
    q975=function(x) unname(quantile(x,.975)),
    mcse=posterior::mcse_mean, rhat=posterior::rhat,
    ess_bulk=posterior::ess_bulk, ess_tail=posterior::ess_tail))
}
compare_parameters <- function(stan, reference) {
  a <- summarize_parameters(stan)
  b <- summarize_parameters(reference)
  z <- merge(a,b,by="variable",suffixes=c("_stan","_reference"),sort=FALSE)
  z$difference <- z$mean_stan-z$mean_reference
  z$combined_mcse <- sqrt(z$mcse_stan^2+z$mcse_reference^2)
  z$mcse_units <- z$difference/z$combined_mcse
  z$sd_units <- z$difference/z$sd_stan
  z
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compare-probit-reference
#| eval: !expr run_probit_validation
reference_original <- run_reference_draws(Ycat, treat1)
# Supply a local source archive to build_corrected_jomo() to avoid downloading.
corrected_library <- build_corrected_jomo()
reference_corrected <- run_reference_draws(Ycat, treat1, library = corrected_library)
comparison_original <- compare_parameters(
  probit_fit$fit$draws(c("beta", "Omega")), jomo_array(reference_original))
comparison_corrected <- compare_parameters(
  probit_fit$fit$draws(c("beta", "Omega")), jomo_array(reference_corrected))
knitr::kable(comparison_corrected[, c("variable", "mean_stan", "mean_reference",
                                    "difference", "combined_mcse", "mcse_units")],
             digits = 4)
# Also inspect posterior SDs, interval endpoints, R-hat, and both ESS estimates:
comparison_corrected
```

### Recorded comparison (26 October 2026)

This snapshot used R 4.6.1, CmdStanR 0.9.0, CmdStan 2.39.0, posterior 1.7.0,
and jomo 2.7-6. Stan used four chains, 1,500 warmup iterations per chain,
and 2,000 retained sampling iterations per chain after the step-size cap;
its warmup seed was 20261026 and sampling seed 20261027. Both reference
runs used four chains per arm with seeds 123436 through 123439, 100,000
burn-in sweeps, and one million further sweeps, retaining every 100th.

**The corrected reference agrees with the paper-targeted Stan model:** the largest
absolute posterior-mean difference was 2.09 combined MCSEs across all 30 parameters.
The maximum absolute differences were 0.0036 for coefficients and 0.0062 for correlations.
Posterior SDs differed by at most 2.4%, and the largest difference between
corresponding 95% interval endpoints was 0.150 Stan posterior SDs.
These are Monte Carlo comparisons, not a proof of equality of the two algorithms.

The unmodified reference differs systematically: the placebo Week 1 coefficient
is -1.742 versus -1.956 in Stan (83.0 combined MCSEs). The corrected value is -1.952.
The two source-level corrections were applied together; this experiment does not
attribute every discrepancy separately to one correction or the other.

|Sampler        | Maximum R-hat| Minimum bulk ESS| Minimum tail ESS|
|:--------------|-------------:|----------------:|----------------:|
|Stan           |        1.0017|             3441|             4816|
|Corrected jomo |        1.0072|             1320|             1987|
|Original jomo  |        1.0016|             2252|             3399|

Stan had **0 divergent transitions**, 0 maximum-treedepth hits, and E-BFMI
between 0.925 and 0.971 in the retained chains. R-hat and ESS above summarize
only the ten coefficients and twenty distinct correlations. Initial warmup
rejections are not counted as retained-chain divergences. These diagnostics
support this example; they do not guarantee adequate sampling on a new dataset.

All reference coefficients in the following tables have been sign-reversed.
“Difference / MCSE” is $(\bar\theta_{\mathrm{Stan}}-\bar\theta_{\mathrm{corrected}})/
\sqrt{\mathrm{MCSE}_{\mathrm{Stan}}^2+\mathrm{MCSE}_{\mathrm{corrected}}^2}$.
The interval columns describe the Stan posterior, not a Monte Carlo confidence interval.

The independent bivariate identity check had maximum absolute error 3e-15.
For the one-visit example (7 responses among 20 patients), the numerical posterior
mean was -0.392807 versus -0.382052 in Stan (MCSE 0.006725); posterior SDs were 0.289319 and 0.285921.
The log-quantile comparison with R had maximum absolute error 7.1e-15 over log
probabilities from $-10^{-16}$ to $-10^6$. Both the one-visit fit and the
covariate/intermittent-missingness fit had zero divergences and zero treedepth
hits; all seven simulated coefficients were inside their 95% posterior intervals.

Before package integration, the remaining work is an imputation-step design and
validation, an adapter to the package design matrices and draw objects, and
broader checks for rare outcomes, larger visit counts, and prior sensitivity.
The fixed integration order and conservative sampler tuning here are prototype
choices, not universal defaults for the package.



### Independent validation checks

Agreement between two samplers is not sufficient on its own. The checks below
also verify the bivariate orthant identity, the one-visit posterior against
numerical integration, and the data mapping for a covariate-adjusted model with
intermittent missingness and an entirely missing subject. The simulation uses a
shared correlation matrix and checks coverage of the known coefficient vector;
it is a small implementation check, not a simulation study of operating
characteristics. Rejection of flat priors for separated cells or custom designs,
and preservation of matrix dimensions during extraction, are also checked.

```{r}
#| label: validate-probit-independent
#| eval: !expr run_probit_validation
model <- probit_model

# Deterministic two-visit orthant check, including all four sign patterns.
mu <- c(-.7, .3)
Omega <- matrix(c(1,.6,.6,1),2)
L <- t(chol(Omega))
signs <- as.matrix(expand.grid(c(-1,1),c(-1,1)))
err <- apply(signs,1,function(s) {
  p1 <- pnorm(s[1]*mu[1])
  value <- integrate(function(u) {
    e1 <- -s[1]*qnorm(u*p1)
    p1*pnorm(s[2]*(mu[2]+L[2,1]*e1)/L[2,2])
  },0,1,rel.tol=1e-10)$value
  truth <- as.numeric(mvtnorm::pmvnorm(lower=c(0,0),
    upper=c(Inf,Inf),mean=s*mu,sigma=Omega*outer(s,s),algorithm=mvtnorm::TVPACK()))
  value-truth
})
stopifnot(max(abs(err)) < 1e-8)

# One visit: no augmentation variables; compare against numerical quadrature.
y <- matrix(c(rep(1,7),rep(0,13)),ncol=1)
p <- prepare_probit_data(y,rep(1,nrow(y)))
stopifnot(p$data$U==0L,p$data$R==20L,p$data$P==1L)
f <- fit_probit_draws(p,model,chains=4,iter_warmup=500,iter_sampling=2000,seed=883L)
sm <- summarize_parameters(f$fit$draws("beta"))
density <- function(b) exp(7*pnorm(b,log.p=TRUE)+13*pnorm(-b,log.p=TRUE))
constant <- integrate(density,-Inf,Inf)$value
exact_mean <- integrate(function(b) b*density(b),-Inf,Inf)$value/constant
exact_sd <- sqrt(integrate(function(b) (b-exact_mean)^2*density(b),-Inf,Inf)$value/constant)
stopifnot(abs(sm$mean-exact_mean) < 4*sm$mcse,
          abs(sm$sd-exact_sd) < .02)
ex <- extract_probit_draws(f,10)
stopifnot(length(ex$beta)==10L,length(ex$sigma)==10L,
          identical(dim(ex$sigma[[1]][[1]]),c(1L,1L)),
          ex$sigma[[1]][[1]][1,1]==1)

# Data preparation: arbitrary missing patterns, all-missing subjects, custom X.
set.seed(443)
N <- 180L; D <- 3L
arm <- rep(1:2,each=N/2)
x <- rnorm(N)
X <- array(0,c(N,D,7L))
for (i in seq_len(N)) for (j in seq_len(D)) {
  X[i,j,j] <- 1
  X[i,j,3+j] <- arm[i]==2
  X[i,j,7] <- x[i]
}
truth <- c(-.6,-.3,.1,.4,.5,.6,.3)
Sigma <- matrix(c(1,.55,.3,.55,1,.4,.3,.4,1),3)
eta <- matrix(matrix(X,N*D,7L)%*%truth,N,D)
Z <- eta + matrix(rnorm(N*D),N,D)%*%chol(Sigma)
Y <- 1L*(Z>0)
Y[matrix(runif(N*D)<.2,N,D)] <- NA
Y[1,] <- NA
p2 <- prepare_probit_data(Y,arm,X,same_cov=TRUE,beta_sd=2)
stopifnot(1L %in% p2$excluded_subjects,p2$data$G==1L,
  all(p2$data$sign_y==2*Y[p2$cells]-1),
  isTRUE(all.equal(p2$data$X,
    sapply(1:7,function(k) matrix(X[,,k],N,D)[p2$cells]),check.attributes=FALSE)))
stopifnot(inherits(try(prepare_probit_data(Y,arm,X,beta_sd=0),silent=TRUE),"try-error"),
  inherits(try(prepare_probit_data(matrix(0,10,2),rep(1,10)),silent=TRUE),"try-error"))
f2 <- fit_probit_draws(p2,model,chains=4,iter_warmup=1000,iter_sampling=1500,seed=884L)
sm2 <- summarize_parameters(f2$fit$draws("beta"))
stopifnot(all(sm2$rhat < 1.01),all(sm2$ess_bulk > 400),
  all(truth > sm2$q025 & truth < sm2$q975))

list(bivariate_errors = err, univariate = cbind(sm, exact_mean, exact_sd),
     synthetic = cbind(sm2, truth))
f$fit$diagnostic_summary()
f2$fit$diagnostic_summary()
```

The log-quantile helper is checked separately against R's tail-aware `qnorm`,
including probabilities whose ordinary floating-point representation underflows.
Writing Stan's output at 18 significant figures is necessary for this numerical
check; rounding CSV output must not be mistaken for function error.

```{r}
#| label: validate-probit-log-quantile
#| eval: !expr run_probit_validation
code <- strsplit(probit_stan_code, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
code <- code[seq_len(which(code=="data {")[1]-1L)]
code <- c(code,"data { int<lower=1> N; vector[N] lp; }",
          "generated quantities { vector[N] q; for (i in 1:N) q[i] = std_normal_quantile_log(lp[i]); }")
m <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model(cmdstanr::write_stan_file(code))
lp <- c(-1e-16,-1e-10,-.1,log(.5),-2,-36+1e-8,-36-1e-8,-50,-100,-700,-1000,-1e6)
f <- m$sample(data=list(N=length(lp),lp=lp),fixed_param=TRUE,chains=1,iter_sampling=1,refresh=0,sig_figs=18)
q <- as.numeric(posterior::as_draws_matrix(f$draws('q'))[1,])
truth <- qnorm(lp,log.p=TRUE)
z <- data.frame(lp,q,truth,error=q-truth)
print(z)
stopifnot(max(abs(z$error))<1e-9)

```
